# Description

## Business context / goal

When an applicant's travel is booked speculatively, the company pays for a *dummy* ticket that is refundable by policy. If the refund is never requested or never lands, the company has simply paid for a flight nobody took and nobody chased.

This check audits the dummy tickets charged in a window, follows each one to its outcome, and opens a case where the money did not come back.

**Expected outcome:** a dummy ticket the company paid for and never got back is surfaced per applicant, at its `ticket_amount_in_aed`, instead of being absorbed silently.

An AI verifier reads the ERP paper trail behind each red flag and returns an advisory verdict. The verdict never changes a case's state; only a human closes a case.

## Trigger & schedule

**Scheduled.** Monthly, on the 15th at 06:00 Asia/Dubai. Each run audits the *previous full calendar month* — payments need time to settle, so the two-week lag is deliberate.

No webhook, no manual trigger, no inbound endpoint of any kind.

The conversion is **already applied**: the workflow was unpublished first, then `Run Monthly` added, the workflow timezone set to `Asia/Dubai`, and the webhook trigger, its two respond nodes and all three callbacks disabled. The disabled nodes are removed from the shipped export by `strip-erp-lease.mjs`, so the production artifact has no inbound endpoint at all. See `records/webhook-to-schedule-conversion.md`.

## Inputs & data sources

ERP production only (`erpbackendpro.maids.cc`). **Read-only — the flow writes nothing back to ERP.** 1 endpoint across 53 nodes:

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | /accounting/transactions/page/advancesearchNew | The dummy-ticket expense population, and the all-time reversal lookup (2 nodes: `Get Dummy Ticket Transactions`, `Get All-Time Refunds`) |

Per-applicant ticket detail is read through the same run; no database, no files, no Snowflake.

### Known route exceptions

- `/accounting/transactions/page/advancesearchNew` — on the 2026-08-25 dead-end route ban. Previously disclosed here as **Section A, no alternative**; that is **no longer true**, so the ERP-team dependency is **withdrawn**. The legacy `POST /accounting/transactions/page/advancesearch` accepts a bounded id list — `[{"property":"id","operation":"in","value":[...]}]` — and returns exactly those rows, 120 verified in a single call on 2026-08-30. That is the targeted accessor whose absence made the original route a dead end. Rewiring to it is recommended but is **not** a blocker for this deployment: the flow runs correctly as it stands.

## Outputs & recipients

- **Google Sheet** — [results workbook](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/172R3JzxXm1nf6Vc3qTesin7eys-jT0ng3SOxUsf3LD8/edit?gid=1358016816#gid=1358016816). One row per audited applicant plus a run log.
  Three Google Sheets nodes write it: `Cases -> Sheet`, `Run Summary -> Sheet`, `Verdicts -> Sheet`.
- **No callbacks.** The three callback nodes present today are deleted as part of the conversion — results are delivered to the workbook and nowhere else.
- TODO — notification e-mail recipient, if any. No Gmail credential is wired on this flow.

Nothing is written back to ERP. No client-facing messages.
